events.title: Cisco Systems, Inc. v. Doe I, et al. (24-856) Order
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted the motion of the Solicitor General to participate in oral argument as amicus curiae and for divided argument in the case of Cisco Systems, Inc. v. Doe I, et al. This procedural order allows the Solicitor General to present arguments on behalf of the United States government during the oral proceedings.
events.why_relevant: The participation of the Solicitor General as amicus curiae can influence the Court's understanding and decision-making in the case.

events.title: Monsanto Co. v. Durnell, John L. (24-1068) Order
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted the motion of the Solicitor General to participate in oral argument as amicus curiae and for divided argument in the case of Monsanto Co. v. Durnell, John L. However, the motion of Roundup and Paraquat MDL Court-appointed Leadership for leave to participate in oral argument as amici curiae and for divided argument was denied.
events.why_relevant: The order is relevant because it records the federal government's formal participation in Supreme Court argument.

events.title: Mullin, Sec., DHS, et al. v. Doe, Dahlia, et al. and Trump, President of U.S., et al. v. Miot, Fritz E. L., et al. (25-1083, 25-1084) Order
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted the motion of petitioners to file the joint appendix in an 8½- by 11-inch format. Additionally, the Court granted in part the respondents' motion for divided argument and for enlargement of time for oral argument, allotting a total of 80 minutes divided as follows: 40 minutes for petitioners, 20 minutes for respondents in No. 25-1083, and 20 minutes for respondents in No. 25-1084.
events.why_relevant: The allocation of time for oral arguments and the format of submissions can affect the presentation and consideration of the cases.

events.title: Supreme Court releases opinion in Chevron USA Inc. v. Plaquemines Parish (24-813)
events.summary: The Supreme Court released an official slip opinion in Chevron USA Inc. v. Plaquemines Parish. Docket number(s): 24-813.
events.why_relevant: The Supreme Court's official opinion in Chevron USA Inc. v. Plaquemines Parish is a primary legal source. Supreme Court opinions can define binding national law and alter the legal position of the executive branch, federal agencies, states, litigants, and democratic institutions.
